tie_grouping: Sort ascending; greedily group values within absolute tolerance of the group's minimum. Use midranks. A tie means membership in the same group, consistently for every metric. This avoids nontransitive pairwise tolerance chains; two adjacent values closer than tolerance may lie across a group boundary.
tolerance_reason: One thousandth of a ps is a prespecified numerical resolution for this analysis, not an estimate of Mapping repeatability. No sensitivity threshold search is performed. This differs from the original pilot's scale-dependent quantization; old metrics are not overwritten.
pairwise_accuracy: correct / (correct + wrong + predicted_tie_on_true_distinct); true ties excluded. No half credit for predicted ties. Also report decisive-only accuracy separately.
top1: Among the minimum predicted tie group choose the smallest frozen integer combination index, without consulting labels. A hit is membership in the minimum actual tie group.
top1_tie_supplement: Report top-set size, uniform random tie-break expected hit and regret, and best/worst regret within that set. These are supplementary, not primary top1 accuracy.
regret: Actual selected delay minus minimum raw actual delay, in ps and percent of the minimum. Do not zero small differences. The optimum is only within the eight frozen combinations.
undefined_correlations: Per-case Spearman and Kendall tau-b are null if either series is constant. Primary aggregate mean and median replace undefined with zero, retain all circuits, and explicitly label zero filling. Additionally report defined-only means and counts. Undefined pairwise accuracy stays null with its defined count, never a fabricated zero.
aggregation: Equal circuit weight within each seed. Equal seed weight within each learned variant; fixed evaluated once. No cross-circuit ranking. Report every seed and full ranges; no seed selection.
scope: Reuse existing v3 validation labels only, including serialized-noop measurement confounding and validation checkpoint-selection dependence. No new independent test, training, inference, candidate generation or Mapping. Exclude train, historical domain, serialized noop and development combinations. Do not use other-branch labels.
